{
  "_comment": [
    "Site-specific configuration for the dropbox.com homepage replica.",
    "The pipeline scripts are URL-agnostic; all site knowledge lives here."
  ],

  "targetUrl": "https://dropbox.com",
  "slug": "dropboxcom",
  "port": 3307,

  "_captureMode": [
    "'rendered' is required here and the decision must be made on a DOM-level",
    "probe, not on the 'auto' element-count ratio. Verified this run:",
    "index.static.html ships 0 <video> elements and an empty security",
    "quote-cards grid, so a static build silently loses both."
  ],
  "captureMode": "rendered",

  "settleMs": 3500,
  "scrollSettleMs": 90,
  "links": "absolute",

  "codegen": {
    "_skipStylesheets": [
      "Dropbox links an UNCOMPILED SCSS source from <head> (// comments,",
      "$font_weight_book: 400). Browsers CSS-error-recover; webpack postcss",
      "hard-fails with 'Unknown word'. Safe to skip only because the compiled",
      "twin sheet redefines the same 15 @font-face rules / 75 url()s.",
      "Filename hash is capture-bound - re-confirm it after each capture."
    ],
    "skipStylesheets": ["font_sharp_grotesk-vflwgPRUu.scss"],

    "_dropSelectors": [
      "This key REPLACES the template defaults rather than merging, so the",
      "defaults are repeated verbatim below, then 4 site-specific entries:",
      "the CCPA consent banner, two marketing/blank iframes, and the",
      ".mov/hvc1 <source> siblings (the hero .mov alone is 134MB and no",
      "harness browser ever selects it - the .webm siblings are what play)."
    ],
    "dropSelectors": [
      "script",
      "noscript",
      "iframe[src*=\"googletagmanager\"]",
      "iframe[src*=\"doubleclick\"]",
      "iframe[src*=\"facebook\"]",
      "iframe[src*=\"hubspot\"]",
      "#onetrust-consent-sdk",
      "#CybotCookiebotDialog",
      "#cookiescript_injected",
      ".ot-sdk-container",
      "#usercentrics-root",
      "#hs-web-interactives-top-anchor",
      "#intercom-frame",
      ".intercom-lightweight-app",
      "#drift-frame-controller",
      "#crisp-chatbox",
      "#tawkchat-container",
      ".grecaptcha-badge",
      "next-route-announcer",
      "[data-replica-drop]",
      "#ccpa-iframe",
      "iframe[src*=\"marketing.dropbox.com\"]",
      "iframe[src=\"about:blank\"]",
      "source[type*=\"quicktime\"]"
    ]
  },

  "viewports": null,

  "_extraAssets": [
    "dropbox.com declares its favicon with the legacy two-token form",
    "rel=\"shortcut icon\". The template's ref matcher now handles that, so this",
    "is belt-and-braces: pinned, explicit, and costs nothing. Without a local",
    "copy the browser probes /favicon.ico at the origin root and logs a 404",
    "that the viewport audit counts as a console error (no baseline path)."
  ],
  "extraAssets": [
    "https://cfl.dropboxstatic.com/static/metaserver/static/images/favicon.ico"
  ]
}

Everything checks out: 3 reveal pairs matching what I noted, with the entry-animation classes appearing across two indexed groups, plus the scroll rail cards and media container all confirmed. The inline iteration-index variable confirms CSS drives the stagger timing rather than JavaScript, and the nav dropdown-open class is also verified in the CSS.

Now I need to trace two CSS variables controlling dropdown heights — the mobile accordion max-height and the desktop current-height variable. The mobile one seems to be referenced but I never saw where it's actually defined, so it's probably set inline via JS just like the desktop variable; I should search for its definition to confirm.

I'm also cataloging the video markup — autoplay, muted, looping videos with a webm source and an empty mp4 source tag, which is likely just an unused fallback placeholder rather than a dropped attribute.

Since the live site has this same empty source, keeping it matches faithfully, and Chromium will still select the webm first. I also note the JSX uses `muted` as an attribute, but that won't reliably set the DOM property, so I'll need the dropboxVideos module to handle it properly. Next I need to check the generated CSS and TSX for specific nav-related classes and definitions, then look at the nav trigger button implementation.

The real fix for the console errors is the empty-src fallback source tags -- React warns when an empty string is passed to a src attribute, even though the live site likely has the same empty sources without triggering a warning since it's not React-rendered. Only genuinely transferable knowledge belongs here — site-specific trivia goes in the per-project note. Merge into this file; never clobber it. Later runs merged in: coframe.com (`coframecom-1`/`-2`/`-3`), rust-lang.org, cash.app/bank (`cashappbank-1`), dropbox.com (`dropboxcom-1`). ## The single biggest trap: rendered-DOM capture bakes in runtime state Capturing the **rendered** DOM (necessary for SPAs) means the page's JavaScript has already run and mutated it. That mutation is invisible in a screenshot but fatal in codegen: - Runtime classes: `faded-in`, `aos-animate`, `is-inview`, `swiper-initialized`, `swiper-slide-active`, `w--current`, `is-loaded`, `splitting`. - Runtime inline styles: `opacity`, `transform`, `transition`, `visibility`, `will-change`. Ship those as-is and every entrance animation renders **already finished** — or worse, frozen at `opacity: 0`, so entire sections are invisible with no error anywhere. Hence: 1. Codegen sanitizes them out (`codegen.stripClasses` / `stripInlineStyleProps`). 2. `app/ClientRuntime.tsx` re-applies them at the right moment. 3. `tests/generated.test.ts` fails the build if any survive. **If `manifest.json`'s `sanitizer.strippedClasses` is empty on an obviously animated page, the strip list is wrong for that site.** Find the real class names in the captured CSS and add them to config. Do not assume the defaults covered it. ### Runtime **nodes** are the other half of this trap — and stripping can't reach them Classes and inline styles are *state*; a rendered capture also contains whole **nodes** the site's JS created: clones appended into containers, headings split into per-word/per-letter spans, absolutely-positioned overlay clones left mid-animation. No amount of class/style stripping removes a node. They ship as permanent duplicates **and** get regenerated at runtime, so the replica renders the same element twice. The nastiest variant: a transient clone the real site keeps invisible at `opacity: 0` gets baked in, then the sanitizer strips `opacity` (it's in the strip list) while leaving `position`/`z-index` (which aren't) — so a clone the original **never shows** becomes permanently visible on top of real content. That was the coframe.com `coframecom-2` bug: 12 `cloneContent()` overlays at `z-index:9999`, 2 cursor clones, 10 split hero spans. **Fix it at the source, not with more stripping:** `captureMode` (`'auto'|'static'|'rendered'`) selects which HTML codegen builds from. `auto` (the default) uses the pristine pre-JS `index.static.html` whenever it passes **both** ratio tests against the rendered DOM (see the next subsection), which is right for essentially every server-rendered site (Webflow/WordPress/Framer/Astro/Next SSG). Only a genuine client-rendered SPA needs `rendered`. Codegen prints the choice and both ratios — read that line. Setting `static` on coframe.com (ratio 0.82) eliminated all baked runtime nodes at a stroke. When genuinely stuck on `rendered`, two config-driven passes remove them generically: `codegen.emptySelectors` (ship a runtime-clone **host** childless) and `codegen.unwrapSelectors` (replace a runtime **wrapper** with its own children, restoring pristine text so the site's script can re-split it). Both are inert until you name selectors. Note these two alone were **not sufficient** on coframe.com — they can only remove what you thought to enumerate; `captureMode` removes the entire category. ### `auto` must judge assets separately from elements — element count is a bad proxy The `static` vs `rendered` decision originally compared raw **element counts** only. That is insufficient, and the failure is visually catastrophic while every automated gate stays green. On cash.app/bank the static file had **97% of the elements** (way over the 0.7 threshold) but only **5 of 31 images** — the promo-card `` nodes are injected client-side after hydration, into `

# Website replica — dropbox.com → `dropboxcom-2`

Run date: 2026-09-16. Target `https://dropbox.com` (homepage), slug `dropboxcom-2`, **port 3307**.
Launch: `cd dropboxcom-2 && npm run dev` → http://localhost:3307

Second run against this site (`dropboxcom-1`, port 3306, was the first). Written to stand on its
own: under the skill's "never build from another run" rule a future run may **not read this
folder's code** — and may not read `dropboxcom-1`'s either. Everything below came from this run's
own capture plus the `dropboxcom-1` *note*.

## Headline: the site had NOT rotated its hashes, and only one new bug appeared

Every hashed CSS-module name the previous run recorded still matched this capture **exactly**
(`_card_1b963_1`, `_cardEntryAnimation_1b963_1`, `_cardShow_1b963_8`, `_scrollArea_bb0ya_5`,
`_mediaContainer_thadj_29`, `_mediaContainerVisible_thadj_62`, `_ticker_90hav_23`,
`_quoteCardsGrid_thadj_158`, `dwg-*`). Carrier counts identical too (9 / 3 / 1). So the previous
note's selectors were reusable verbatim — but they were still **re-derived from this run's own
`scroll-reveals.json` and asserted by tests**, which is what makes that claim checkable rather
than assumed. Do the same next time; do not trust the hashes on faith.

## Final gate results (all green)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `vitest` | 3 files, **68 tests** pass (34 of them the new `tests/dropbox.test.ts`) |
| `next build` | clean (only autoprefixer `flex-end` + webpack cache-serialization warnings) |
| `npm run viewports` | **PASS: 0 problem viewports out of 7** — 0 hidden-content, 0 console errors, 0 remote requests, 0 broken images (77 images), 0 duplicate visible headings |
| `npm run compare` (full, both directions) | mean **14.85%**, 7 viewports, **134 slices**, height delta ≤2.09% |

No `replica.baseline.json` was needed — the file does not exist in this folder. Per-viewport
compare means: iphone-se 20.68, ipad-mini 22.40, ipad-pro 15.62, laptop 12.94, iphone-14-pro
11.31, pixel-7 10.91, desktop-wide 10.11.

## THE NEW BUG THIS RUN: empty `src=""` → 4 console errors → 7/7 viewport FAIL

Not hit by `dropboxcom-1` (that run's `viewports` passed first time), so this is new knowledge.

- **Symptom:** `npm run viewports` failed **7/7** with `-> console-errors`, 4 identical errors per
  viewport: *"An empty string ("") was passed to the %s attribute. This may cause the browser to
  download the whole page again over the network."*
- **Cause:** each of the 4 product `<video>` elements carries an **empty mp4 fallback**,
  `<source src="" type="video/mp4" />`, in Dropbox's real markup. React (dev) warns once per
  element. It is **not** a capture defect and not a missing asset.
- **Why it must be fixed, not baselined:** `console-errors` has **no baseline path** in
  `scripts/viewport-check.mjs` (unlike `overflow` / `hiddenContent` / `duplicateVisibleText`).
- **Fix:** added `source[src=""]` to `codegen.dropSelectors` and re-ran `npm run codegen`.
  Verified: `grep -c 'src=""'` went 4 → **0** while `<video>` stayed 4 and `type="video/webm"`
  stayed 4; `third-party nodes dropped` 7 → 11. Then `viewports` → PASS 0/7.
- **Zero pixel cost:** an empty `src` is never selected by the browser's media-source algorithm,
  so the `.webm` sibling is what played before and after.
- **Useful detail:** codegen's mini selector matcher **does** support empty-value equality.
  `parseSelector`'s regex captures `""` as `''`, and `matchesSelector` does `val !== a.value`
  after an `undefined` check, so `source[src=""]` matches only genuinely-empty attributes and
  cannot catch the real `.webm` sources.

## `replica.config.json` — what was set and why

- `captureMode: "rendered"` — decided by a **DOM probe** (throwaway `scrape/probe-capture-source.mjs`),
  not the `auto` ratio line. Measured static vs rendered this run: elements **1519/1673 = 0.908**
  (would have *passed* the 0.7 element test), but `<video>` **0/4**, `<iframe>` 0/3, `<svg>` 27/39,
  `<source>` 20/31, and `div._quoteCardsGrid_thadj_158` ships **0 children vs 3**. A static build
  would silently lose all 4 product videos and the whole quote-cards row.
- `codegen.skipStylesheets: ["font_sharp_grotesk-vflwgPRUu.scss"]` — Dropbox links an
  **uncompiled SCSS source** from `<head>` (`//` comments, `$font_weight_book: 400`). Browsers
  error-recover; webpack postcss hard-fails with `Unknown word`. Re-confirmed present and
  unchanged this run; manifest records it as `"status": "SKIPPED"` with the matching `skipRule`.
  The compiled twin (`vendor-15-font_sharp_grotesk-vflRd2mZl…css`) carries the real `@font-face`
  rules, so nothing is lost. **The single "1 stylesheet could not be localised" warning printed by
  codegen IS this sheet — expected, not an error.**
- `codegen.dropSelectors` — **this key REPLACES the template defaults instead of merging**, so the
  defaults are repeated verbatim, then **5** site-specific entries: `#ccpa-iframe`,
  `iframe[src*="marketing.dropbox.com"]`, `iframe[src="about:blank"]`,
  `source[type*="quicktime"]`, and the new `source[src=""]`.
- `extraAssets: ["https://cfl.dropboxstatic.com/static/metaserver/static/images/favicon.ico"]` —
  belt-and-braces; the template's `rel` token-list matcher fix (from `dropboxcom-1`) is present in
  `scripts/lib/assets.mjs`, so the favicon would now be found anyway. No favicon 404 this run.
- `settleMs: 3500`, `scrollSettleMs: 90`, `links: "absolute"`, `viewports: null`.

## Effects: `ClientRuntime.tsx` registers exactly 4

Hand-written modules in `app/lib/`: **`dropboxReveals`**, **`dropboxNav`**, **`dropboxVideos`**,
plus generic **`smoothAnchors`** (2 real anchors: `#main-content`, `#manage-cookies`, neither a
widget control). Also needed: **`types/dropbox-component-attrs.d.ts`**, a types-only augmentation
of React's `HTMLAttributes<T>` for the genuine `label`/`tag` attributes Dropbox's `dwg-*`
components put on `<a>` (≈50 × TS2322 without it). Do not strip them — real upstream markup.

**10 generic effects deliberately NOT registered.** 8 censused to zero targets against the
generated markup (`fadeIn`, `navScroll`, `navDropdown`, `tabs`, `accordion`, `counters`,
`lazyImages`, `forms` — note `features.json` reports 77 "lazyImages" but they are native
`loading="lazy"`, needing no JS). Two match real elements and are **actively harmful**:
`navToggle` (applies `is-open`/`nav-open` classes this site's CSS never defines; would fight
`dropboxNav`) and `marquee` (the logo ticker `._ticker_90hav_23` is already CSS-animated via
`@keyframes _keyframes-standard_90hav_1` over already-duplicated markup; cloning desyncs the wrap).
That reasoning is written into `ClientRuntime.tsx` so a future run doesn't helpfully re-add them.

### `dropboxReveals.ts` — 3 gating pairs, and the clipped-rail trap

| base selector | visible class | n | group |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.dwg-multi-block-card-entry-animation` | `…--is-visible` | 9 | — |
| `._card_1b963_1._cardEntryAnimation_1b963_1` | `_cardShow_1b963_8` | 3 | `._scrollArea_bb0ya_5` |
| `._mediaContainer_thadj_29` | `_mediaContainerVisible_thadj_62` | 1 | — |

The quote cards sit in an `overflow-x: scroll` rail (grid ~2304–2932px wide depending on
viewport) so the third card is **outside the clip window**. IntersectionObserver computes
intersection *through* that clip while `rootMargin` inflates only the root rect — a wide margin
does **not** fix it. Hence per-pair `groupSelector`, trigger = `el.closest(groupSelector) ?? el`
(the `?? el` is the hash-rotation fallback), bucket targets by trigger, observe the trigger at
**`threshold: 0`** (a rail that wide never reaches a fractional ratio). One-shot (`unobserve`
after reveal); `prefers-reduced-motion` reveals everything immediately. **No JS stagger** — the
capture ships inline `--dwg-iteration-index` and the CSS turns it into `animation-delay`.
This run's `viewports` reported **0 hidden-content findings at all 7 viewports**, which is the
runtime proof the rail reveal works.

### `dropboxNav.ts` — two CSS variables exist in NO captured stylesheet

`--dwg-nav-item__dropdown-max-height` (<1280px) and `--dwg-nav-current-dropdown-height` (≥1280px)
are written **inline by the site's own JS**; they appear in none of the 122 captured sheets. Left
unset, a dropdown "opens" to zero height. The module sets **both** from the panel's `scrollHeight`
(which reports full content height despite `max-height: 0; overflow: hidden`). 6 triggers
(`button[aria-haspopup="true"][aria-controls]`) → panels by `aria-controls` id →
`.dwg-nav-item__dropdown--open`. Also drives `.dwg-nav__dropdown-background` **height** (the
desktop panel itself is transparent, so without this the dropdown reads as floating text),
`.dwg-nav--dropdown-opened` on the nav root (gates the per-link stagger), the mobile burger
(`.dwg-nav__hamburger-button` → `.dwg-nav-mobile-dropdown--open`), `.dwg-nav__overlay--open`, and
the body scroll lock `body--dwg-nav-mobile-dropdown-open--universal` (released on teardown).
Closes on Escape and on outside click; handlers `preventDefault()` + `stopPropagation()`.

### `dropboxVideos.ts` — `muted` must be a DOM property

Sets `muted` / `defaultMuted` / `playsInline` as **properties** (a JSX `muted` attribute alone
does not permit autoplay — the browser reads the property), then `.play()`, retrying on
`canplay`/`loadeddata`, swallowing the expected autoplay rejection. Scoped to `video[autoplay]`
so a video the original didn't autoplay stays paused. 4 `.webm` videos.

## Tests: `tests/dropbox.test.ts`, 34 tests

Behaviour (via the jsdom IntersectionObserver mock in `tests/setup.ts`: `triggerIntersection`,
`observerOptionsFor`, `observedElementCount`, `resetObservers`) **plus drift assertions that
re-derive from build artifacts**: exact carrier counts 9/3/1, the visible class absent from the
capture, the rail still present, 6 × `aria-haspopup="true"` / 6 × `aria-controls="nav-item-…"`,
6 dropdown panels, 1 burger, 1 mobile dropdown, 4 `<video>` / 4 `autoPlay`, every video source a
local `/assets/` path — and that all 4 effects are **registered** in `ClientRuntime.tsx` while
`navToggle`/`marquee` are **not**. A rotated hash therefore fails the suite instead of silently
blanking the page. jsdom has no layout, so panel `scrollHeight` must be stubbed via
`Object.defineProperty`.

## Residual visual difference (14.85% mean) — all explained, nothing missing

Judged for **block presence**, not just score, on all 7 composites opened with `read_image`
(laptop y=0 / 5434 / 8151; ipad-mini y=0 / 4372 / 5465 / 9837):

- **Live-only CCPA cookie dialog** — the largest single contributor, a big opaque panel in *every*
  live slice by design (`#ccpa-iframe` dropped). Permanent expected residue.
- **A/B headline.** Capture froze *"One place to store, share, and finish the job"*; live served
  *"…and collaborate"* at laptop/ipad-mini this run. Multivariate across runs — a mismatch here is
  not a stale capture.
- **Scripted demo + video motion phase.** The share/permissions demo was caught at different
  stages (local "Link copied to Final_files" vs live hover; local "Reference Folder → People/Links"
  vs live one step along). Both sides correct, different frames — and it doubles as proof autoplay
  works.
- **Live-only footer locale row** (`English (United States)` + globe `<svg>`) is injected
  post-capture, so it cannot be in generated output; it shifts the lower footer between the two
  sides (visible in the ipad-mini y=9837 composite).
- **Page height:** max delta **2.09%** (laptop: local 9240 vs live 9051). Live-side variance, not a
  local layout bug — local is *identical* (9240px) at both laptop and desktop-wide, while **live**
  reported 9051 vs 9267 at those same two widths in the same run.
- **Direction deltas** at laptop y=1811/2717/4528 and desktop-wide y=2160/4320 are motion phase:
  **every slice pair in the whole report has `misalignedBy: 0`**, so both sides reached identical
  offsets. `liveLoadSuspect: false` on all 7 viewports.
- **Fidelity positive:** nav bar, subcopy, both CTAs, the "700 million registered users" line and
  all six footer link columns render **grey** (identical) in the diff channel.

## Two "looks broken, is actually faithful" traps re-confirmed

1. **`body font Times New Roman`** in the viewport audit is **correct**. `npm run viewports --live
   --only=laptop` reported *the same* `Times New Roman` for the live site. Dropbox never sets a
   family on `body`; `h1`/`p` get the real Sharp Grotesk / Atlas Grotesk stacks (self-hosted
   `@font-face` present in `vendor-02/03/09/10/14/15`). Do not "fix" this.
2. **Live's own console is dirty.** The `--live` laptop run showed **11 console errors** (incl.
   `xtp.init is not a function`, a 404) and **27 failed requests** (grpc, bttrack pixels). Live is
   a reference, never a gate; only the local count must be 0.

## Housekeeping: ~147MB of unreferenced `.mov` deleted

`source[type*="quicktime"]` drops the `<source>` nodes but `npm run scrape` still downloads the
files. Confirmed **zero `.mov` references anywhere in `app/`** (generated TSX + CSS + metadata),
then deleted 4 files from `public/assets/video/` (hero alone **135MB**; total ~147MB, taking
`public/assets` from 252MB down). **`scrape/raw/video/` still holds the same 4 files (~147MB)** —
left in place deliberately as the capture cache. Re-running `npm run scrape` re-downloads the
`public/` copies; delete them again.

## Start here next time

1. Read this note, then `npm install`, then `npm run pipeline`.
2. Expect, all already solved above: the SCSS build-killer, `captureMode: rendered` (probe it,
   don't trust the ratio), the `dwg-*` attribute types, the two runtime-only nav height vars, the
   `muted` DOM-property trap, the clipped card rail, **the empty `src=""` console errors**, and the
   `.mov` bulk.
3. Re-derive the 3 reveal pairs from *your* `scrape/analysis/scroll-reveals.json` and let the drift
   tests confirm the hashes — they had not rotated between run 1 and run 2, but that is luck, not a
   guarantee.
4. Port 3306 = `dropboxcom-1`, 3307 = `dropboxcom-2`. Use 3308 next.

That mutation is invisible in a screenshot but fatal in codegen: 16| 17|- Runtime classes: `faded-in`, `aos-animate`, `is-inview`, `swiper-initialized`, 18| `swiper-slide-active`, `w--current`, `is-loaded`, `splitting`. 19|- Runtime inline styles: `opacity`, `transform`, `transition`, `visibility`, `will-change`. 20| 21|Ship those as-is and every entrance animation renders **already finished** — or worse, frozen 22|at `opacity: 0`, so entire sections are invisible with no error anywhere. Hence: 23| 24|1. Codegen sanitizes them out (`codegen.stripClasses` / `stripInlineStyleProps`). 25|2. `app/ClientRuntime.tsx` re-applies them at the right moment. 26|3. `tests/generated.test.ts` fails the build if any survive. 27| 28|**If `manifest.json`'s `sanitizer.strippedClasses` is empty on an obviously animated page, 29|the strip list is wrong for that site.** Find the real class names in the captured CSS and add 30|them to config. Do not assume the defaults covered it. 31| 32|### Runtime **nodes** are the other half of this trap — and stripping can't reach them 33| 34|Classes and inline styles are *state*; a rendered capture also contains whole **nodes** the 35|site's JS created: clones appended into containers, headings split into per-word/per-letter 36|spans, absolutely-positioned overlay clones left mid-animation. No amount of class/style 37|stripping removes a node. They ship as permanent duplicates **and** get regenerated at runtime, 38|so the replica renders the same element twice. 39| 40|The nastiest variant: a transient clone the real site keeps invisible at `opacity: 0` gets 41|baked in, then the sanitizer strips `opacity` (it's in the strip list) while leaving 42|`position`/`z-index` (which aren't) — so a clone the original **never shows** becomes 43|permanently visible on top of real content. 540|## Verification that actually catches things
541|
542|Beyond tsc/build/tests, the browser audit gates on: horizontal overflow, oversized elements,
543|burger/desktop nav swap at the breakpoint, canvas backing-store *and* paint state, animation
544|trigger counts pre/post scroll, carousel init, broken images, console errors, failed requests,
545|and **any remote request at all**. The last one is what keeps "self-hosted" honest over time —
546|and it was the only gate that would have caught the entity-decoding bug above.
547|
548|Assertions must not over-constrain: `assets.total > 0` and `stylesheets.length > 0` are wrong,
549|because a page with no external sub-resources or no CSS is a legitimate, fully-replicated page.
550|Assert the *reconciliation* (per-kind counts sum to the total; `@import` list equals the manifest
551|list) instead of a magnitude. Also scan `metadata.ts` for remote origins, not just `.tsx`/`.css` —
552|that gap is exactly how the remote-icon leak survived a green test run.
553|
554|**A "0 broken images" pass does not mean the right images.** The viewport audit checks
555|`naturalWidth > 0`, which a wrong-but-valid asset satisfies perfectly. Two separate real bugs
556|on cash.app/bank (empty black figure boxes, desktop art on phones) sailed through it. Broken-ness
557|and correctness are different properties; only the pixel diff covers the second.
558|
559|**Smoke-test on a content-rich site, never a trivial one.** example.com (1 section, 0 assets,
560|1 inline sheet) passed every gate while three separate real bugs sat in the pipeline; rust-lang.org
561|(197 elements, 8 sections, 219 assets, 2 webfont families, 4 stylesheets) surfaced all of them
562|within one run. A trivial target exercises neither the splitter, nor the cascade rebuild, nor the
563|asset downloader.
564|
565|**Hand-written bridge tables deserve a derivation test, not a review.** Any table mapping
566|capture artifacts to runtime paths (video sources, responsive image variants) is transcribed by
567|hand and fails *silently* when wrong — a blank box or a wrong-but-valid image, no console error.
568|Write the test so it re-derives the table from `__NEXT_DATA__` / `asset-map.json` /
569|`app/generated/*.tsx` and compares, rather than asserting hand-copied literals; and assert every
570|referenced file exists in `public/`. This caught nothing on the day it was written and is exactly
571|what protects the next re-scrape, when content hashes change.
572|
573|### Don't sample a moving value across two tool calls
574|
575|Seconds of real time elapse between a `browser` click and the follow-up `inspect`. If a 4s
576|autoplay timer is mutating the thing you're reading, the second call returns a *different*
577|moment — and reading it as the click's result invents bugs that don't exist. This cost two
578|speculative "fixes" on one run before the misdiagnosis was caught.
579|
580|Assert an **invariant** that holds at every instant instead of an exact expected value:
581|`activeTab === activePane`, `location.hash === ''`, `scrollY` drift `=== 0`,
582|`getAnimations().length === 1`. Those are true regardless of when the sample lands.
583|
584|Also: **Playwright's click does its own scroll-into-view**, which shows up as a one-off `scrollY`
585|change that looks exactly like a page-side autoscroll bug. Distinguish them by clicking a second
586|already-visible element — harness-caused drift goes to 0, a real anchor hijack keeps firing.
587|
588|### Verify a negative grep before acting on it
589|
590|A grep that finds nothing is weak evidence, because the pattern may simply be wrong. A
591|character class excluding commas/newlines missed `.nav-dropdown.visible` rules that were
592|tab-indented inside media queries, which nearly led to "the CSS is missing, the port is broken"
593|and a wrong fix. Re-check with a looser second pattern (or count raw substring occurrences)
594|before concluding something genuinely is absent.
595|
596|**The `grep` tool only searches the open workspace.** Pointing it at an absolute path outside
597|(e.g. `~/.klenny/skills/website-replica/template/...`) returns **0 matches**, which reads
598|exactly like "the code isn't there". Use `run_command` with shell `grep`/`sed`, or `read_file`,
599|for anything outside the project. I briefly mistook this for the template lacking a fix it did
600|have — a false negative of precisely the kind the rule above warns about.
601|
602|## No gate catches a "won't stay scrolled" bug
603|
604|`tsc`, vitest, `next build`, the 7-viewport gate and the visual compare were all green with the
605|coframecom-1 autoscroll bug present. Screenshots can't show it and the viewport harness never
606|idles ~4s in one spot. **Verification recipe:** park on the carousel until its active tab
607|advances on its own (autoplay is armed by an `IntersectionObserver` needing ~50% visibility),
608|*then* scroll well past it, wait 3+ ticks, and assert `window.scrollY` unchanged **and**
609|`location.hash` still empty. Jumping straight past the section proves nothing — autoplay never
610|arms, so the timer that causes the bug never runs.
611|
612|Related standing rule: the sanitizer **strips `webflow.js`**, so nothing suppresses widget
613|hrefs in a replica. (1) Never let a generic anchor/scroll effect bind a widget control.
614|(2) **Any handler you hand-write for a widget control must call `preventDefault()` itself.**
615|These two mask each other — fixing only one swaps a smooth scroll-back for an instant hash-jump,
616|an identical-looking symptom. And a stripped `webflow.js` means the nav dropdown + mobile menu
617|must be **hand-written**, not ported.
618|
619|## Gotchas that are NOT template bugs (don't "fix" these)
620|
621|- **`animations N-1/N` off-by-one is usually a false positive.** `viewport-check.mjs`
622|  intentionally counts a broad selector (`.fade-in, [data-fade], [data-aos], [data-animate],
623|  [data-scroll]`). Webflow sites often carry a bare authoring attribute like `data-fade=""` on an
624|  element the site's own script never queries. Check what the captured script's selector actually
625|  is before chasing it.
626|- **"N css url() ref(s) could not be mapped" is usually a false positive.** Confirmed again on
627|  cash.app/bank: all 22 named files were present. Spot-check a few and let runtime 404s arbitrate.
628|  (But see the one-sheet-concentration exception above.)
629|- **Don't add `width`/`height` to `stripInlineStyleProps` globally.** Some inline sizing is
630|  genuinely authored (canvas elements). If codegen bakes a *runtime-written* capture-time width
631|  into markup and it causes overflow, fix it in the effect module by clearing that element's
632|  inline size once at init.
633|- **A `ResizeObserver` callback that unconditionally mutates its own element will hang the
634|  Playwright harness** (`npm run viewports` stalls right after its header, looking like a
635|  stray-browser issue). Memoize last-written values and bail early.
636|- **A wide-viewport `compare` regression is often the LIVE side flaking** — see above; run it
637|  twice.
638|- On Windows, `pkill -f` silently fails against node/chrome. Use `netstat -ano | grep LISTENING`
639|  or `wmic process where "commandline like '%…%'" get processid`, then `taskkill //PID <pid> //F`.
640|  Always confirm a rebuilt server actually restarted (`EADDRINUSE` -> you may be measuring a
641|  stale server). Confirm teardown positively: `curl` returning code `000` (connection refused)
642|  is the proof, and remember leftover `node.exe`/`chrome.exe` in `tasklist` may be the editor and
643|  the user's own browser, not your run.
644|
645|## Operational notes
646|
647|- Chromium: reuse the cached `ms-playwright` install via `playwright-core` (no second browser
648|  download). `scripts/lib/chromium.mjs` covers Win/macOS/Linux + `headless_shell` fallback and
649|  prints the install command when absent. **Throwaway probe scripts must import from
650|  `scripts/lib/chromium.mjs` (`findChromium()`/`launch()`)** — the template vendors
651|  `playwright-core` only, so a bare `import { chromium } from 'playwright'` fails.
652|- `scripts/viewport-check.mjs` **never spawns a server** — it navigates to `--url` (default
653|  `localhost:3300`). Kill the server before running the gate and you get 7×
654|  `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, which looks like a catastrophic regression and isn't. Start
655|  `npx next start -p <port>` first.
656|- The `browser` tool's `inspect`/`snapshot` need the **`tab` param**. Omitting it silently
657|  targets the default `main` tab (`about:blank`) and returns an empty-DOM result that mimics a
658|  hydration failure.
659|- **`node -e "require('/c/Users/...')"` fails under Git Bash** — Node's Windows module loader
660|  can't resolve the MSYS-style path, and the `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` looks like a missing/broken file.
661|  Use a `C:/...` path (forward slashes are fine) with `fs.readFileSync` + `JSON.parse`.
662|  `node --check <file>` is the quick syntax gate after editing template scripts.
663|- Asset filenames: hash-suffix them (sha1 of the URL) — real sites serve many distinct files
664|  named `logo.svg`, and naive basename collisions silently overwrite each other.
665|- Asset downloads are cached; `--force` to bypass. Codegen fully overwrites `app/generated/`,
666|  so re-running the pipeline is always safe — and note this is *why* a bad sheet can't be fixed
667|  by hand-deleting it.
668|- `extraAssets` (top level of `replica.config.json`) downloads URLs the capture browser never
669|  requested — the escape hatch for media-query-selected variants, and the clean way to self-host
670|  a favicon. Document *why* each entry is there with a `_extraAssets` comment block; a future run
671|  will otherwise "tidy" them away.
672|- Keep the port in `replica.config.json` only (`scripts/dev.mjs` reads it), so the dev server
673|  and the verification scripts can never disagree about it. Pick a fresh port per run so a
674|  previous replica's server can't be measured by mistake. (Used so far: 3300–3304.)
675|- `next.config.mjs` is read only at boot: restart the dev server after touching it, or you'll
676|  measure the old behaviour and conclude the fix didn't work.
677|- **`npm start` serves the built bundle**: after editing any client module, rebuild AND restart
678|  before re-testing in the browser, or you'll be testing the previous bundle and "confirm" a fix
679|  that never shipped.
680|- Grep dev-server logs for 404s only after restarting the server post-fix; a long-lived log
681|  mixes pre- and post-fix requests and will send you chasing already-fixed problems.
682|- Codegen writes **everything** to `app/generated/` (sections, `index.css`, `vendor-NN`/
683|  `inline-NN` sheets, `metadata.ts`, `manifest.json`). Keep `config.mjs`'s `appStyles` and
684|  `appGenerated` pointing at the same directory — the app scaffold and tests both assume it.
685|- Beware `*/` inside a JSDoc block comment (e.g. writing `data-*/aria-*`): it closes the comment
686|  early and corrupts the rest of the file into a syntax error that looks unrelated.
687|- Delete large binaries with shell `rm`, not `delete_file` — the latter dumps the whole binary
688|  diff into context. (Also true for a pile of throwaway probe scripts at the end of a run; and
689|  drop never-fetched heavy variants, e.g. 4 unused `.mov` files = 155MB on dropbox.com, keeping
690|  only the `.webm` the page actually uses.)
691|- **Propagate template-level fixes to `~/.klenny/skills/website-replica/template/` before
692|  finishing**, then `node --check` each touched file and add the knob to
693|  `replica.config.example.json`. A fix that lives only in the project copy is a fix the next run
694|  re-discovers from scratch.
695|

### An *empty* attribute is inert in the browser but a hard console error in React

Real markup contains deliberately-empty attributes. dropbox.com gives each of its 4 `<video>`
elements an empty mp4 fallback — `<source src="" type="video/mp4">` — alongside the real `.webm`.
The browser's media-source algorithm never selects an empty `src`, so it costs **zero pixels**;
but React (dev) logs *"An empty string ("") was passed to the src attribute"* once per element,
and `npm run viewports` failed **7/7 on `console-errors`** — one of the few checks with **no
baseline path** in `viewport-check.mjs` (unlike `overflow` / `hiddenContent` /
`duplicateVisibleText`). So it has to be *fixed*, not tolerated: drop the inert node via
`codegen.dropSelectors` (`source[src=""]`), then re-verify the real sources survived (`src=""`
count 4 → 0 while `<video>` stays 4 and `type="video/webm"` stays 4).

The mini selector matcher **does** support empty-value equality: `parseSelector`'s `[attr=value]`
regex captures `""`, and a missing attribute reads back `undefined` before the `!==` compare, so
the selector cannot catch a populated `src`. Check that before assuming you need a code change.

Generalises well past this one attribute: **a console-error gate promotes any cosmetically
harmless markup quirk into a hard failure**, so when a gate trips, first establish whether it is
even baselineable — if it isn't, stop looking for a tolerance and go remove the cause.

## Done — `dropboxcom-2` is complete, all 8 gates green 🐾

A pixel-faithful, fully self-hosted Next.js + TypeScript replica of **https://dropbox.com** now lives in `dropboxcom-2/`. Run it with `cd dropboxcom-2 && npm run dev` → **http://localhost:3307**.

### Final gate results

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `vitest` | 3 files, **68 tests** pass (34 new, in `tests/dropbox.test.ts`) |
| `next build` | clean (only autoprefixer/webpack-cache warnings) |
| `npm run viewports` | **PASS — 0 problem viewports of 7**; 0 console errors, **0 remote requests**, 0 broken images (77), 0 hidden content |
| `npm run compare` | mean **14.85%** across 7 viewports / 134 slices, both directions; height delta ≤ 2.09% |

### How it was built

1. **Scaffold + config** from the pristine template (never from the earlier `dropboxcom-1` run — only its memory note), port 3307.
2. **Pipeline** captured 122 stylesheets, 77 images, 4 videos, 6 nav dropdowns.
3. **`captureMode: "rendered"` was decided by a DOM probe, not the `auto` log line.** The element ratio was 0.908 and would have *falsely passed* the 0.7 threshold — but the static capture ships **0 of 4 `<video>`** elements and the quote-cards grid with **0 children instead of 3**. A static build would have silently lost all four product videos and an entire section.
4. **Hand-wrote three effect modules** (the site's own JS is stripped): `dropboxReveals` (3 gating pairs; the quote-card rail is `overflow-x: scroll`, so IntersectionObserver must watch the *rail* at `threshold: 0` — `rootMargin` can't fix a clip), `dropboxNav` (sets two CSS variables that exist in **none** of the 122 captured sheets because the site writes them inline at runtime — without them every dropdown opens to zero height), and `dropboxVideos` (`muted` must be a DOM *property*, not a JSX attribute, or autoplay is refused). Plus `types/dropbox-component-attrs.d.ts` for Dropbox's genuine `label`/`tag` attributes (~50 × TS2322 without it).
5. **Censused all 12 generic effects** — 8 matched zero targets, and 2 (`navToggle`, `marquee`) matched real elements but were *actively harmful*; the reasoning is written into `ClientRuntime.tsx` so a future run doesn't helpfully re-add them.

### The one real bug this run, and its fix

`npm run viewports` initially failed **7/7** on `console-errors`. Cause: each `<video>` carries an empty mp4 fallback, `<source src="" type="video/mp4">`, which React warns about once per element — and `console-errors` is one of the few checks with **no baseline path**, so it had to be fixed rather than tolerated. Added `source[src=""]` to `dropSelectors` (verified the matcher supports empty-value equality, so it can't catch the real `.webm`), re-ran codegen (`src=""`: 4 → 0, videos still 4/4), then verify and viewports both went green.

### Two "looks broken, is actually faithful" traps I did **not** 'fix'

- **`body font-family: Times New Roman`** — a `--live` run reported *the same thing* for the real site. Dropbox never sets a family on `body`; `h1`/`p` get the real Sharp Grotesk stacks.
- **Live's own console is dirty** (11 errors, 27 failed requests). Live is the reference, never a gate.

The residual 14.85% was traced block-by-block across 7 composites I actually opened: the live-only CCPA cookie dialog (intentionally dropped, the single biggest contributor), a multivariate A/B headline, demo/video motion phase, and a live-only footer locale row. Every slice pair had `misalignedBy: 0` — no missing or broken sections.

### Cleanup & knowledge capture

- Deleted **~147MB of never-played `.mov` files** from `public/assets/video/` after confirming zero `.mov` references anywhere in `app/` — `public/assets` went **252MB → 105MB**. `scrape/raw/` keeps its copies as the capture cache.
- Dev server torn down: **port 3307 free**, no orphaned `node.exe`/`chrome.exe`.
- Wrote the project memory note, and **merged** 5 additions into the global lessons note — reading all 695 lines off disk first, since the earlier read truncated and rewriting from a partial copy would have clobbered content.
- **Propagated the fix upstream** into the template (`source[src=""]` in `DEFAULT_DROP_SELECTORS` + a `_dropSelectors` doc block noting the key *replaces* rather than merges the defaults), validated with `node --check` and a JSON parse — so the next run inherits it instead of rediscovering it.

Good code, good boy — that one's worth a treat. 🦴

## Objective
- Build a pixel-faithful Next.js/TypeScript replica of https://dropbox.com (triggered by `website_url: https://dropbox.com`) as a new workspace subfolder, following the `website-replica` skill procedure, with zero remote requests at runtime.

## Important Details
- Slug is `dropboxcom-2` (an earlier run `dropboxcom-1` exists on port 3306 and per the skill's hard rule may **not** be read as source — only its memory note may be used); this run's port is `3307`.
- `captureMode: "rendered"` confirmed via custom DOM probe: static vs rendered elements 1519/1673 (0.908, would falsely pass a 0.7 threshold) but video 0/4, iframe 0/3, svg 27/39, source 20/31, quote-cards grid 0 vs 3 children.
- `codegen.skipStylesheets: ["font_sharp_grotesk-vflwgPRUu.scss"]` — Dropbox serves an uncompiled SCSS source in `<head>`; confirmed `SKIPPED` (not an error) in manifest.json this run too.
- `codegen.dropSelectors` — template defaults repeated verbatim (key replaces, not merges) plus **5** site-specific entries (updated from 4): `#ccpa-iframe`, `iframe[src*="marketing.dropbox.com"]`, `iframe[src="about:blank"]`, `source[type*="quicktime"]`, and newly added `source[src=""]` — the last one added mid-run to drop the inert empty mp4 fallback `<source>` on each of the 4 videos, which React warns about ("An empty string... was passed to the src attribute") and which the viewport audit's `console-errors` gate (no baseline path) was failing on. Verified this selector syntax is supported by `codegen.mjs`'s custom `parseSelector`/`matchesSelector` (regex-based, supports `[attr=value]` incl. empty string, strict `!==` compare, absent attrs return `undefined` so real `.webm` sources are never caught).
- `extraAssets` includes the Dropbox favicon URL as belt-and-braces.
- `settleMs: 3500`, `scrollSettleMs: 90`, `links: "absolute"`, `viewports: null`.
- Effects kept in `ClientRuntime.tsx`: `dropboxReveals`, `dropboxNav`, `dropboxVideos`, generic `smoothAnchors` (2 real anchors). Effects dropped (documented in file header comment): 8 with zero targets (`fadeIn`, `navDropdown`, `tabs`, `accordion`, `counters`, `lazyImages`, `forms`, `navScroll`) + 2 harmful-if-matched (`navToggle`, `marquee`).
- `types/dropbox-component-attrs.d.ts` added to widen React's `HTMLAttributes` with `label`/`tag` (Dropbox's `dwg-*` components render these non-standard attrs on real `<a>` elements; without this, `tsc` throws ~50× TS2322).
- Confirmed via live-viewport check that `body font: Times New Roman` is **not a defect** — the live site itself reports the same font under this measurement, so it's a baseline artifact, not a regression.
- Confirmed a live-only CCPA/cookie consent dialog is the dominant contributor to per-slice diff percentages in the compare sweep (correctly dropped locally, appears in composites as a large live-only colored block).
- Found **294MB of unreferenced `.mov` files** (both `public/assets/video/` and `scrape/raw/video/`, each ~147MB: hero 135MB + 3 smaller clips) — zero references in `app/generated`; decided to delete only from `public/assets/video` (the shipped payload), leaving `scrape/raw` alone since it's the capture cache and codegen doesn't read the video bytes directly, only `scrape/raw/index.html` and the asset-map.
- Never build from/read another run's code (`dropboxcom-1`) — only the pristine template and this run's own folder.

## Work State
### Completed
- Checklist items 1–7 all marked done via `update_checklist`:
  1. Scaffold + replica.config.json.
  2. `npm install` (126 pkgs) + `npm run pipeline` (122 stylesheets, 77 images, 4 videos, 6 dropdowns) — exit 0.
  3. Capture artifacts read; `captureMode: rendered` confirmed via custom probe script.
  4. Hand-wrote `app/lib/dropboxReveals.ts`, `app/lib/dropboxNav.ts`, `app/lib/dropboxVideos.ts`, `types/dropbox-component-attrs.d.ts`; rewrote `app/ClientRuntime.tsx` — all via successful `write_file` calls (confirmed by diffs in tool results) after the earlier `multi_write` failure was resolved by splitting into separate `write_file` calls.
  5. Wrote `dropboxcom-2/tests/dropbox.test.ts` (461 lines, 34 tests covering reveal behaviour, drift-vs-generated-markup, nav open/close/Escape/outside-click/mobile sheet, video muted-property/retry/no-op/throw-safety, and "every effect actually registered" checks).
  6. `npm run verify` passed clean (tsc, 3 test files / 68 tests, `next build`) on first pass.
  7. Started dev server on port 3307 (confirmed HTTP 200).
  8. Ran `npm run viewports` — **initially FAILED 7/7** on `console-errors` (4× React "empty string passed to src attribute" warnings traced to `<source src="" type="video/mp4">` fallback tags on all 4 videos, confirmed via grep).
  9. Diagnosed root cause, added `source[src=""]` to `dropSelectors`, re-ran `npm run codegen` (confirmed 0 remaining `src=""`, 4 videos/4 webm sources intact), re-ran `npm run verify` (exit 0, 68 tests) and `npm run viewports` (**PASS: 0/7 problems**).
  10. Ran `npm run compare` (full, both directions): exit 0, **mean 14.85%** across 7 viewports / 134 slices, comparable to prior run's 14.74%. `liveLoadSuspect: false` on all 7 viewports; 0 non-zero `misalignedBy` entries anywhere.
  11. Reviewed 8 composite images via `read_image` (laptop y0/y5434/y8151; ipad-mini y0/y4372/y5465/y9837) — every discrepancy traced to expected causes: live-only cookie/CCPA dialog, differing demo-animation phase/timing, or minor footer/locale-row offset; no missing content or broken sections found.

  13. Identified 294MB of unreferenced `.mov` files via `run_command` (find/ls) and confirmed zero `.mov` references in `app/generated`.

I still need to verify static ships all the essentials: it captured 9 videos, 4 tab panes, and 1 dropdown, but everything's under one big section wrapper. There's also a custom cursor element that appears to be created at runtime rather than existing in the static HTML, plus dot-train, trail-particle, and propeller classes tied to the hero section, all pointing to a heavy custom JS animation layer likely driven by inline scripts that codegen may have dropped — I need to check the inline script dump in the analysis summary to recover that logic, and also look into the unmapped CSS url() warnings, including an unresolved import to a design-tokens package.

blocks.text:
The comparison between static and rendered versions looks great - video and source elements match exactly, and most other counts are close, with the main difference being an iframe from marketing/OneTrust that only appears in the rendered version.

The rest of the counts confirm static is the right choice: everything except runtime-generated elements (letter-trail spans, app-cursor, OneTrust consent widget, route announcer) matches perfectly. This means the letter-trail animation doesn't exist in static markup at all — it's built by JS splitting some source element into 127 individual letter spans, so I need to find what element in static gets targeted for that split.

There's also a cursor-trail effect with particles attached to a custom cursor overlay that only appears on mouse movement, which Playwright won't trigger — likely invisible in screenshots but worth porting for fidelity. I'm outlining the main work items now: reconstructing the letter-trail source and JS behavior, and handling the various reveal-on-scroll states across intro points, feature cards, tabbed banner, and video players.

I also need to build a video module that plays videos when they enter the viewport since none have autoplay attributes — the site controls playback itself via a data attribute. There's also a hero propeller video that swaps to a static still image after scrolling, and a tab system with four tabs and matching panels to reproduce.

For the tabs, since they're implemented as buttons with aria-controls rather than anchor links, a generic tab initializer should work fine without scroll-hijack concerns. I also notice a mega nav with dropdown menus and many aria-expanded states — this needs its own module handling hover/click behavior, sticky positioning, and mobile burger toggling, though the burger count is showing zero in the feature scan.

I'm also spotting a country selector with listbox behavior and a disclaimer accordion tied to aria-controls. Since OneTrust consent scripts get stripped in the static capture, there's no banner to worry about locally, but the live site will show one — that's expected residue when comparing. Now I need to track down where the actual site behavior lives, which should be in the Next.js JS chunks, so I'm going to dig through those files to find the logic for the letter-trail effect, reveals, video, and tabs.

I'm planning to grep across the 58 captured JS assets for class names like letter-trail, is-revealed, is-inview, data-letter-index, playback-owned, propeller, trail-particle, and dot-train, while also reading through features.json and cross-checking the generated markup and TSX source for the letter-trail, video-player, tabs, and nav structures. I should also check the lib index and tests directory to understand the effect contracts available.

I'll skip the jsdom approach for now and just grep the raw HTML directly for "letter-trail" with surrounding context to see the structure, alongside reading features.json, checking app/lib and app/generated, and searching JS chunks for related class names.

The probe is decisive: **static is the right source**. All reveal carriers and media are complete in static (video 9/9, source 18/18, `.intro__point` 3/3, `.features__card` 9/9, `.video-player` 8/8), while rendered's extra ~300 elements are purely runtime artifacts — **127 `.letter-trail__letter` split spans**, `.app-cursor`, `next-route-announcer` and OneTrust's 113 nodes. Baking those in is exactly the trap my notes warn about.

Now I need to recover the site's own behaviour from its JS chunks.

I now have the full engine and need to plan what's next. I've discovered that the custom CSS classes like letter-trail, app-cursor, hero__propeller, and others aren't present in any of the generated CSS files, even though scroll-reveals.json quoted specific styling rules for them — meaning those definitions likely came from captured CSS in the raw scrape data rather than being embedded in the generated stylesheet.

Something's off, since codegen reported 21 stylesheets in cascade order but my grep across all generated CSS files, including the large vendor bundles, came up completely empty for these class names. I'm now considering whether the page's actual CSS is hiding somewhere in scrape/raw/css that never made it into the generated output.

That points to a serious gap: maybe the page's own stylesheet is only injected client-side via a dynamic import, so the static-mode capture skipped it entirely, leaving the hero and feature sections unstyled. I need to track down exactly which raw CSS file contains these classes and whether it's linked in the static HTML at all, since that determines whether I need to switch capture modes or find another fix.

That `onloadeddata` inline handler will trigger a React console error since it's not a recognized event property, so I need to find a way to strip inline `on*` attributes at the template level since codegen's selector-drop mechanism won't work on individual attributes.

The plain `on="interacted"` attribute is different though—React just renders unrecognized lowercase attributes as-is without warning, so that one's harmless.  But `onloadeddata`, `onclick` and similar startsWith-"on" attributes likely trigger "Unknown event handler property" console errors, which I should verify empirically rather than guess. The `ontext="[object Object]"` cases (60 occurrences) look suspicious too, possibly stringified objects leaking into an attribute somewhere.

Actually, on closer inspection those matches are false positives — my regex is catching substrings of longer attributes like `aria-controls` or `data-context`, not real `on`-prefixed handlers. So the only genuine inline handler in the codebase is `onloadeddata`, which is the one thing I need to address.

I also notice the tabbed-banner panels are all marked `is-active` in the static capture — the SSR renders every panel as active since the JS's select(0) call is what actually narrows it to just the first one at runtime. Without that JS running, my replica would show all four panels simultaneously, causing duplicate headings and broken layout, so I need to make sure my tabs module calls select(0) to replicate that behavior.

I'm also noticing the discover carousel is built on Flickity, referenced through the disclaimer.js export.

build, with page dots always active there, while features/trust cards use carousel behavior only under a mobile breakpoint. Faithfully replicating this means the discover section needs Flickity at all widths, otherwise it'll just render as a static horizontal track instead.

I still need to check disclaimer.js for the bundled Flickity version, plus trace through several unlabeled helper functions (H, W, K, X, Q, j) that appear to handle accessibility wiring, dot initialization, and the card-cursor hover effect — I'll need to read through that file to figure out what each one does.

Given the file is 52KB minified, my best approach is to grep for the specific function or class definitions of each minified symbol (Yt, Zt, ee, ie, se, ne, te, Kt) so I can trace their actual implementations rather than guessing at their purpose.

I want to prioritize whatever most affects visibility and layout: staggered card reveals with a one-shot intersection observer, the banner's in-view toggle, and the video player's visibility class tied to an observer with a -20% bottom margin, applied across all eight video players.

There's also a letter-trail effect splitting headline text into individually animated letters — without porting it, the heading just renders fully visible as plain text, which is safe but loses fidelity, whereas porting it risks a hidden-content gate if the animation stalls partway.  I'm leaning toward porting it faithfully since the source code is fully available to rewrite into readable form, given it's such a signature part of the page.

Wait, the hero actually intercepts wheel/touch/keydown events and prevents default until the animation resumes — it's a genuine scroll-lock at load, which is critical to replicate since the compare sweep might scroll differently than a real wheel event and bypass this behavior entirely.

There's also a scroll listener that watches scrollY and force-finishes the hero animation once past a threshold, and a scrollIntoView jump to #intro that could disrupt the sweep if triggered mid-scroll — I need to make sure this doesn't wreck the screenshot alignment during comparison.

I also notice the freeze() function sets the body background to white, plus dim/is-dimmed handling. This is turning into a substantial port with roughly five modules: the hero entry and propeller with its scroll gating and chevron logic, the letter-trail with dot train and particles, the prefooter video players with playback sync, and the tabbed banner component.

Beyond those I still need reveal animations for staggered elements and in-view video playback, a hover-only card-cursor effect for the prefooter's "Find out more" interaction, and the Flickity-based discover carousel plus mobile carousels for feature and trust cards. There are also five unidentified inits in disclaimer.js I still need to trace — likely candidates are the accordion, country selector, and nav behaviors.

But before writing anything, I need to resolve the missing page CSS issue first, since that overshadows everything else — if the page's own stylesheet isn't being emitted, nothing else will matter. So my plan is to check which raw CSS file contains the letter-trail styles and whether it's linked correctly in static versus rendered output, review the head-order file to see the actual stylesheet order, check how codegen collects stylesheets and whether it strips attributes like onloadeddata, and finally trace the disclaimer.js function definitions to identify those five mystery symbols.

Major red flag spotted: **none of the page's own CSS classes** (`letter-trail`, `app-cursor`, `hero__propeller`, `video-player__replay`, `tabbed-banner__tab`, `reveal-headline`) appear in any emitted stylesheet, even though `analyze` quoted their rules from the capture. That would mean the page-specific stylesheet never made it into the build — which dwarfs every other issue. Investigating that first, plus the disclaimer.js helpers.

Privately: I need (1) which raw CSS holds those rules and whether it's linked in static vs rendered, (2) head order + manifest sheet list, (3) how codegen collects sheets and whether it can drop the `onloadeddata` attribute, (4) the definitions of disclaimer.js's exported inits + Flickity version, (5) the discover/features carousel markup. All independent — requesting together.

I'm confirming intelligence.css is properly linked in the static head and the raw file exists with all custom rules, but codegen only emitted 21 stylesheets while the static head lists 16 stylesheet links plus the custom one, so something's being dropped in the generation step.

Continuing to trace: the last three sheets (fonts.css second occurrence, disclaimer.css, intelligence.css) don't appear in codegen's output at all, yet there's no explicit "missing sheet" warning — just the unrelated URL-mapping warning. This suggests codegen is rebuilding the stylesheet cascade from head.json rather than the actual rendered head, and those three sheets simply aren't present in that head data source, which is why they get silently skipped.

Now I'm reasoning through where these missing links actually live in the DOM — likely inside the body, injected by the CMS as body-level `<link rel="stylesheet">` tags, not in the head. Codegen appears to handle inline body `<style>` blocks but never accounts for body-level stylesheet links, which is a template-wide gap causing these three sheets to vanish from the replica. I want to confirm this by checking exactly where those links sit in the static HTML and inspecting how capture.mjs builds head.json and body styles, plus how codegen assembles its stylesheet list.

I'll write a quick inline node check to find the byte positions of `<body` versus the three CSS link tags, and also inspect head.json's contents directly. I also want to jot down the identified helper functions I've traced so far — scroll lock, cursor creation, click-fade, pointer tracking, and disclaimer accordion — before circling back to the CSS ordering fix.

Continuing to trace variable names: `te` maps to the card-cursor helper imported from the prefooter module, `Kt` handles syncing video sources to matching media queries, `Zt` is a playback manager class, and `Jt` turns out to be Flickity itself, bundled inline inside disclaimer.js. Since Flickity is bundled rather than pulled from a package, I can't cleanly pin down its exact version — it looks like the older v2.3.0-style API rather than v3.x, so installing the npm package directly is risky and I may need to port just the minimal carousel behavior instead.

Now I'm questioning whether Flickity is even required for the discover carousel at desktop widths — the DiscoverCarousel component always initializes Flickity on the six-cell track regardless of viewport, so I need to check what the CSS does to that track without JS: it might overflow horizontally and fail visually, or it might hold up fine. Similarly, the features and trust card stacks only get Flickity on mobile, so at desktop there's no carousel behavior to worry about, but at mobile without Flickity the cards would just stack vertically per CSS, which could look noticeably different from the live site.

Given the effort constraints, I'll hold off deciding on Flickity until after the CSS fix, then render and visually judge whether it's needed — checking first if intelligence.css already bundles flickity's own styles so I don't need to install the package separately. I'm going to batch a few investigations: locating the three stylesheet links relative to body in the static HTML versus the head.json entries, reading a chunk of codegen.mjs, checking capture.mjs for how body styles and head data get collected, and grepping intelligence.css for flickity and discover__track rules.

The CSS mystery is solved — and it's serious. The static head has **16** stylesheet links, but codegen emitted only **13** link sheets: the last three (`fonts.css` #2, `disclaimer.css`, and crucially **`intelligence.css`** — the entire page-specific stylesheet, holding `letter-trail`, `hero__propeller`, `video-player`, `tabbed-banner`, `app-cursor`) are missing. They aren't in `head-order.txt` either, so they're `<link>`s in the **body**, and codegen rebuilds the cascade from head.json only.

Confirming the exact mechanism before I fix it:

I'm noticing the stylesheet link tags actually survived into the generated JSX file, showing up as preload and stylesheet link elements pointing to the fonts, disclaimer, and intelligence CSS assets.

These paths were localized to `/assets/css/` locations, which means the browser does load the sheets at runtime via those body links, just like the original page. So maybe my earlier "serious bug" assumption was wrong — the codegen's localAsset() must have resolved the hashed filenames successfully, meaning the asset map likely stores the full original URL as the key rather than a short filename, which explains why my earlier substring search for 'intelligence.css' turned up nothing.

I should double check that `public/assets/css/intelligence.e5b1965a.css` actually exists on disk, since the scrape did pull down CSS files. If it's there, the styles load fine at runtime via the body `<link>` tags rather than through the `@import` list — which means `next build` is unaffected since they're static files, though this does create a fidelity gap in the manifest/import reporting, and could introduce ordering or FOUC concerns depending on how browsers handle stylesheet links placed in the body versus the head.

But the actual bug I've found: the codegen only rewrites `url()` references in sheets it directly emits, not in these raw downloaded body-linked files. So `intelligence.css` and `fonts.css` still have dozens of `url()` references pointing at the original Intuit CDN domains, meaning fonts and background images will fetch remotely and break the zero-remote-requests guarantee even though typography looks correct locally. I want to verify this by grepping the downloaded CSS for `https://` references to confirm the un-rewritten URLs are really there.

The proper fix is to route these body-level stylesheet links through the same vendor pipeline as everything else — capturing them, rewriting their `url()`s, inserting them into the `@import` list at the right cascade position, and then removing the original `<link rel="stylesheet">`/preload tags from the JSX so they don't double-load. Since dropping the links without emitting the rewritten sheets would make styles disappear, both changes need to land together — though there might be a simpler alternative worth considering.

Since dropping happens in the JSX walker while the emitted cascade is separate, I should also drop the redundant preload link for the same reason — it'd become a wasted request pointing at a sheet no longer linked, even though harmless. So the plan solidifies: capture.mjs tracks ordered bodyEntries of body-level style/link elements with their href/media, keeping bodyStyles for compatibility, and codegen.mjs's emitStyles gets updated to use this richer data.

I'm now checking whether the mini selector matcher supports chained attribute selectors like `link[rel="preload"][as="style"]`, and deciding to simplify to separate `rel="stylesheet"` and `as="style"` matches instead. But I'm second-guessing whether dropping the body stylesheet link is actually faithful to the original page load, since the app's own CSS import now serves that role.

I'm also worried about postcss choking on the 42KB intelligence.css when it's pulled in via `@import`—if there's an unresolved nested `@import` to a design-tokens variables file inside it, that could break the build the way the earlier SCSS import did.

Before making any changes, I want to verify a few things: whether intelligence.css itself has nested `@import` statements, that the served CSS files actually exist on disk under public/assets/css, and whether the body sheets reference any remote `https://` URLs. I'll gather all of that first.

I also need the asset-map.json structure to see if those URLs are keys, check whether the codegen's selector-matching logic supports the `link[rel="stylesheet"]` pattern with chained attributes, and confirm whether fonts.css covers the fonts actually used across the site.

Important correction to my read: those three body sheets **did** survive into the JSX as `<link>` tags with localised `/assets/css/...` paths — so they do load. The real defect is narrower but still gate-breaking: codegen only rewrites `url()` for sheets it *emits*, so these body-linked sheets are served as raw downloads with their original remote `url()`s (33 + 38 of them → Intuit CDN fonts/images = remote requests), and they're absent from the manifest/@import cascade.

Verifying that precisely before I patch capture/codegen:

---

## **PRECISE BEHAVIOURAL SPEC — Intuit Intelligence Page**

### **1. Hero Word/Propeller Entry Animation**

**Trigger:** `DOMContentLoaded` → `document.fonts.ready` (or fallback timeout 1500ms) → IntersectionObserver on `.hero` (threshold 0, no rootMargin)  
**CSS-only?** NO — JS adds/removes classes and drives timing.

**Sequence:**
- Check `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`; if true, skip animation entirely and enter `enterHold` state.
- JS selects all `.hero__word` and their `.hero__word-inner` children.
- **Delays:** First word delays by `700ms` (`ie`), each subsequent word staggers by `300ms – (300−200ms) × (idx / max)` = `300–100ms` depending on word index.
- At each word's delay, JS sets initial opacity `0` and `transform: translateX(48px)` (or `translateY(6%)` for `.hero__propeller`).
- Then at `delay + 260ms`, JS applies `transition: opacity 260ms ease, transform 300ms cubic-bezier(0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94)` and sets `opacity: 1; transform: none`.
- **CSS handles** the fade/slide-in via the applied transition (keyed on class removal of `is-animating`).
- After final word + `300ms`, call `startPropeller()`.

**Classes:** `.hero` gets `is-animating` on start, removed before word transitions begin.

---

### **2. Propeller Video Playback & Detachment**

**Trigger:** After hero word animation completes (auto-triggered, ~1.5s from entry).

**Logic:**
- If `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, freeze video at 1 second with poster and exit.
- If video hasn't been resumed by user scroll yet: pause video at `1.8s` (`A`) via `timeupdate` listener; switch to `enterHold` state (scroll-lock active).
- If user has already resumed (via scroll), let video play to end naturally (~3s duration).
- **Once resumed (by scroll):** video plays, then on `ended` event calls `settleClip()`.
- **On settle:** Detach video to fixed position (get current bounding rect, replace with placeholder span, move `<video>` to `document.body` as fixed), then after `600ms` transition margin/transform.
- **After `600ms`:** Fly video to `.intro__statement` or fallback element: transform to `translate(offset_x, offset_y)` via `600ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)`.
- Then fade out opacity over `300ms` and freeze.

**Classes on video wrapper:** None directly; video is detached to fixed layer. Placeholder span inserted at `.hero__propeller`.

---

### **3. Hero Scroll-Lock & Release**

**Trigger:** On mount, scroll-lock is armed. Released when:
1. User scrolls > `window.innerHeight × 0.18` (min 120px), OR
2. User presses wheel/keydown/touchmove, OR  
3. Hero animation completes (if not already scrolled).

**Scroll-Lock Implementation:**
- Apply class `"icom-nav-locked"` to `<body>`.
- Set `body.style.overflow = "hidden"` and `body.style.top = -scrollY + "px"`.
- Store scroll position; restore on unlock via `window.scrollTo({top: savedY, left: 0, behavior: "instant"})`.

**Release Sequence:**
- On scroll threshold or input event, call `finishInstantly()` → clears all timers → removes `is-animating` → sets video to playthrough mode → removes scroll-lock.
- Alternatively, wait for video `ended` event → call `settleClip()` → `complete()` → fires `onComplete` callback → removes scroll-lock.

---

### **4. Letter-Trail (Reveal Headline) Animation**

**Trigger:** IntersectionObserver on element with `.reveal-headline` (threshold 0, rootMargin "0px 0px -25% 0px"). On intersection, delay by `startDelay` (default 500ms for intro headline), then play.

**Text Splitting:**
- JS wraps every `.reveal-headline` in a `.caterpillar` div.
- Splits text content by grapheme (`Intl.Segmenter` or `Array.from()`) and wraps each grapheme in `<span class="letter-trail__letter" data-letter-index="{i}">`.
- Wraps each "word" (split by space/punctuation) in `<span class="letter-trail__word">`.
- Sets `aria-label` on root to original trimmed text.

**Animation:**
- Create `<div class="dot-layer">` and `<div class="dot-train">` (position absolute, will-change: transform).
- **Per-letter reveal timing:**
  - Dot-train moves to each letter's center via `animateTo()` with `110ms linear` easing.
  - After dot arrives (pause: `20ms` / lookup time for punctuation like `.` = 520ms, `!` = 620ms, `,` = 240ms, etc.), set letter to `opacity: 1` with `110ms` delay.
  - Spawn particle at letter position, animate via Web Animations API over `430ms` with color gradient.
- **Line breaks:** When dot moves to next line, take curved path: up-and-left then down-and-right via 4-point cubic-bezier path over `110ms`.
- **End state:** Remove dot-train, add class `is-filled` to root, set all remaining letters to `is-visible`.

**CSS-only reveal:** Once `.is-visible` is set, letter opacity transitions via `.letter-trail__letter.is-visible { opacity: 1 }` (instant, no transition).

**Reduced motion:** All letters instantly get `is-visible` + root gets `is-filled`.

---

### **5. Tabbed Banner (Tab Selection & Auto-Rotation)**

**Trigger:** `IntersectionObserver` on `.tabbed-banner` (threshold 0.35) to detect visibility.

**Tab Selection Logic:**
- On mount, call `select(0, {resetProgress: true})` to **narrow the initially-active panel** (SSR renders all as `is-active`).
- `select(index)` sets `aria-selected={true}` and `tabindex="0"` on selected tab, removes from siblings.
- Toggles `is-active` class on corresponding `.tabbed-banner__panel`.
- If panel has a `<video>`, get its `VideoPlayer` instance (via WeakMap) and call `setSelected(true)`.

**Auto-Rotation Timer:**
- **Default duration:** 6000ms.
- If active panel has playing video, use video duration; else use 6000ms.
- On `requestAnimationFrame` loop, track elapsed time.
- Set CSS custom property `--tab-progress` (0 to 1) on active tab for progress bar animation.
- **On reach duration or video ends:** auto-advance to next tab via `select((index+1) % tabCount)`.

**Hover/Pause Logic:**
- If `--tabbing-paused: true` (hardcoded `b = false`), pause auto-rotation.
- Hover on active tab or banner pauses rotation; leave resumes after idle 4000ms.
- Keyboard: Arrow keys select tab, press stops auto-rotation.
- Swipe: Left/right swipe on banner selects next/prev tab, stops auto-rotation.

**Classes:** `.tabbed-banner` gets `is-ready` after mount. Active tab/panel get `is-active`. Filling bar via `--tab-progress` CSS variable.

---

### **6. Video Player (In-Panel & Video Source Syncing)**

**Trigger:** Each `.video-player` is wrapped in a `.tabbed-banner__panel`. Instantiated on mount.

**Media-Query Source Swap:**
- Query all `<source media="...">` children, extract media queries, register with `window.matchMedia()`.
- On media-query change (via `change` event or `addListener` for older browsers), re-run `sync()`.
- `sync()` calls `video.load()` to re-evaluate `currentSrc` based on matching `<source>` media query.

**Playback State Sync:**
- `.video-player` only plays if:
  1. Its panel is `is-active`
  2. Panel is visible in viewport (IntersectionObserver threshold 0, rootMargin "0px 0px -20% 0px")
  3. No `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
- If conditions unmet, pause.
- On video `ended` event, add `is-ended` class to video-player (shows replay button).
- Click replay button: reset currentTime to 0, set `restart=true`, call `sync()` again.

**Playback Manager (`PlaybackManager`):**
- Wraps video autoplay logic (permission-gated).
- `setActive(true)`: attempt play; on failure, listen for user gesture (pointerdown, touchstart, keydown) then retry.
- `setActive(false)`: pause.

**CSS:** `.video-player` opacity 0/scale up; on `is-visible` class, transition to opacity 1 via 700ms ease. On `is-ended`, show replay button via opacity/visibility/scale transitions.

---

### **7. Discover & Features Card Carousels (Flickity)**

**Media Query Breakpoint:** `(max-width: 767.98px)` triggers carousel; above, use CSS Grid.

**For `.discover__track`:**
- **Desktop (≥768px):** Flickity **enabled** with `cellAlign: "center", contain: false, pageDots: true, draggable: true`.
- **Mobile (<768px):** Flickity **enabled** with `cellAlign: "left", contain: true, pageDots: true, draggable: true`.
- Add 40px carousel spacer on mobile only.
- Dotted pagination uses custom styling: 6px circles, selected expands to 26px pill.

**For `.features__cards` and `.trust__cards`:**
- **Desktop (≥768px):** CSS Grid (3 columns for features, 2 for trust) — **no Flickity**.
- **Mobile (<768px):** Flickity **enabled** with same options as discover.
- Stagger reveal on desktop: `is-revealed` class applied per card at `index × 300ms` delay via `IntersectionObserver` on container (threshold 0, rootMargin "0px 0px -20% 0px").

**Reflow on breakpoint change:** Destroy/recreate Flickity instance, preserve selected index.

---

### **8. Staggered Card Reveals (Features/Trust)**

**Desktop only.** Trigger: `IntersectionObserver` on `.features__cards` or `.trust__cards` (threshold 0, rootMargin "0px 0px -20% 0px").

Found it — the culprit is a `data-brand-tracking` attribute holding an escaped JSON string. JSX attribute strings don't process backslash escapes like JavaScript does, so those literal backslashes before the quotes are breaking the parser and triggering the invalid character error.

The correct fix is to wrap the value in a JS string expression using braces, so `\"` sequences work properly inside a normal string literal. So codegen should either escape double quotes as HTML entities in double-quoted attributes, or emit the value as a JSON-stringified expression when it contains quotes or backslashes — I need to check how the current escaping logic handles this case.

I should check whether other emitted files besides NextSection.tsx have the same escaping bug, and figure out how widespread the malformed attributes are before editing. I'll grep codegen.mjs for the attribute-serialization function and count occurrences of the bad escape pattern in the output file, then make the fix — using JSON.stringify keeps ampersands literal correctly since it's a JS string expression.

Root cause is now unambiguous. Column 59 on line 30 is a **backslash** (charcode 92):

```
data-brand-tracking="{\"data-wa-link\":\"icom-globalnav:cornerstone-tt\",...}"
```

Codegen JS-escaped a JSON attribute value (`"` → `\"`) inside a **double-quoted JSX attribute**, but JSX attribute strings are HTML-like — they don't honour backslash escapes. So the `\` is an invalid character, the following `"` terminates the value early, and everything after it (`}`, `>`, the element's children) cascades into bogus tokens. That single bug accounts for all 23 tsc errors. Good news: the only non-ASCII in the whole file is `—`, `’`, `©` — all legitimate content, so there's nothing else lurking.
